title: Add a storage that keeps each table in its own file
description: Adds `DirectoryStorage` (`tinydb/directory_storage.py`), which keeps a database as a directory with one JSON file per table instead of one big file, so a database under version control gets small diffs. A table's file is its name with every character that is not safe in a file name percent-encoded, plus `.json`, so any table name works and every file stays inside the directory; reading decodes the name back exactly. Each file is replaced through a temporary file in the same directory, and a write that fails (for example because a document cannot be serialized) leaves every file as it was. Tables that are gone from the database have their files removed; other files in the directory are not the storage's and are left alone. The directory is created when missing, unless `create_dirs=False`, and `read_only=True` never creates or changes anything on disk. Includes tests.

defects.summary: quote() keeps / unescaped by default, so a table name containing ../ writes its file outside the database directory.
rstrip removes any trailing characters from the set '.json', not the suffix, so a table named 'session' reads back as 'sessi' and its file is then deleted as a dropped table.
read_only=True still creates a missing directory, because only create_dirs is checked before os.makedirs.
Each table is serialized just before its file is replaced, so a table that cannot be serialized fails the write after earlier tables' files were already changed.
defects.defective:
for name, docs in data.items():
            text = json.dumps(docs, **self.kwargs)

defects.summary: Every file not starting with a dot counts as a table, so other files in the directory are parsed as JSON and deleted by the next write.

ceiling.summary: _replace removes its temporary file only when the failure is an OSError, so a write that fails for another reason, such as a document the configured encoding cannot represent, leaves a stray temporary file in the database directory.

decoys.why: The temporary file must be in the same directory for os.replace to be atomic, and it is removed on every failure.
Syncing the directory is best effort by design: some platforms cannot open or fsync a directory, and the files themselves were already synced.
